componentPlan.focusQuote: Rivers and lakes are results of runoff.
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The listed figure shows the water cycle, so labeling its named parts connects vocabulary to the visual model.

componentPlan.focusQuote: Of the many processes involved in the hydrologic cycle, the most important are:
componentPlan.pedagogicalReason: The page presents the cycle in order, so tracing stages in sequence builds understanding of continuous circulation.

overview.headline: How water circulates between ground and atmosphere

keyPoints.point: Students learn that the hydrologic cycle involves continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.
keyPoints.quote: The hydrologic cycle involves the continuous circulation of water in the Earth-Atmosphere system.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that evaporation is the change of state from liquid to gas.
keyPoints.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that transpiration is evaporation of water from plants through stomata on leaves.
keyPoints.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that condensation is the process where water vapor is changed into liquid state.
keyPoints.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyPoints.point: Students learn that precipitation can be rain, hail, snow or sleet as fresh water received on Earth.
keyPoints.quote: Precipitation can be in the form of rain, hail, snow, or sleet.

keyTerms.gloss: Change of state from liquid to gas that requires energy input
keyTerms.quote: Evaporation is the change of state in a substance from a liquid to a gas.

keyTerms.gloss: Evaporation of water from plants through leaf stomata controlled by humidity
keyTerms.quote: Transpiration is the evaporation of water from plants through stomata.

keyTerms.gloss: Process where water vapor changes into liquid state in clouds or dew
keyTerms.quote: Condensation is the process whereby water vapor is changed into a liquid state.

keyTerms.gloss: Water falling to Earth as rain, hail, snow or sleet after coalescence
keyTerms.quote: Precipitation is the primary way we receive fresh water on Earth.

keyTerms.gloss: Excess precipitation flowing over saturated ground to form rivers and lakes
keyTerms.quote: Runoff occurs when there is excessive precipitation and the ground is saturated (cannot absorb any more water).

keyTerms.gloss: Small openings on underside of leaves connected to vascular tissues
keyTerms.quote: Stomata are small openings found on the underside of leaves that are connected to vascular plant tissues.

analysis.pageCoverage: The page explains the hydrologic cycle through evaporation, transpiration, condensation, precipitation, runoff, and return flow to the oceans.
